messages:
samir: Heads up — we started seeing missing child spans for a portion of user-facing traces around 07:03 UTC. Root trace exists but downstream services are showing no spans after ingress.
elaine: :eyes: I’m seeing an uptick in dropped spans in the collector logs too. Sample from the logs: "span dropped: missing parent header or invalid traceparent". Correlates with ingress host nginx.
aj: Noted traffic pattern — large header sets on a few requests (cookies + x-redwood-* headers). nginx has `large_client_header_buffers` defaults might be trimming headers, so traceparent could be cut.
samir: That aligns with what I observed. Traces that lose spans have trace IDs matching but no traceparent forwarded. Looks like trace context truncated at the proxy layer.
maria: observability-bot just fired alert: "span-propagation-failure-rate > 3%" starting 07:02 UTC. I’ll open a quick incident page. :warning:
observability-bot: alert: span-propagation-failure-rate (threshold 3%) — hosts: ingress-1, ingress-2 — recent 5m rate: 4.8% — runbook: check proxy header size & collector queue.
kevin: Can someone paste the collector exporter queue metrics? I want to confirm we're not also losing on exporter-side.
aj: Quick check I ran:
```
curl -s http://otel-collector:8888/metrics | grep exporter_queue
# exporter_queue_length 128
# exporter_queue_dropped_total 42
# exporter_queue_push_failures_total 7
```
aj: We have some queue drops but not at scale to explain all missing spans. Primary signal still looks like header trimming.
elaine: Also found nginx error in access log around 07:01: `client intended to send too large header` on a few requests to /api/v1/route — confirms header buffer overflow.
samir: Suggested mitigation: temporarily remove the custom header-merge filter we rolled last week (changed path and added big debug headers). That filter added ~6 headers per request.
maria: I can open a canary rollback to remove the header-merge filter on ingress-1 first. If that removes the errors we can roll to the rest. Anyone object?
kevin: +1, do it. Also add a short-term collector tweak: increase receiver header size and bump exporter queue size from 128->512 to soak the burst.
aj: Command to check live header errors and nginx buffer setting:
```
kubectl -n ingress logs deploy/nginx-ingress -c nginx | grep "too large header" -n
kubectl -n ingress exec deploy/nginx-ingress -- nginx -V 2>&1 | grep large_client_header_buffers
```
maria: Rolling back header-merge filter on ingress-1 now. Deploy-bot: starting deploy rollback (canary) for ingress-filters v2 -> v1.
deploy-bot: rollout: ingress-filters rollback started by maria — canary on ingress-1 (1/3) — est 90s.
elaine: After rollback on ingress-1, I'm seeing immediate reduction in `too large header` errors and traces through that node now include child spans again. :thumbsup:
observability-bot: alert resolved: span-propagation-failure-rate back under 1.2% on ingress-1. Global rate still ~1.9% while we finish rollouts.
samir: Great. Postmortem TODOs: (1) add header size tests to preflight, (2) avoid sending large debug headers in filters, (3) add an OTEL collector metric correlating dropped span count with header-trim events, (4) tune default nginx buffer config across clusters.
maria: I'll own the rollout + postmortem doc. Filing a short doc in #postmortems and linking here. Thanks for fast triage everyone. :beer:
kevin: Also propose a follow-up: make tracer resilient to partial contexts (try to accept trace-id only when traceparent is missing, with a warning) — reduces impact of intermediate header loss (engineering debt ticket).
samir: SGTM. Closing this thread once rollouts complete. Last check in 07:06 UTC shows propagation healthy on canary and ingress-2/3 rolling next.
